title: Understanding Codons
text: Remember that a codon is a sequence of three DNA letters. How many different codons can you form with the letters T, G, C, and A?

title: Compact Representation
text: Think about how you can represent the DNA data in a way that captures the essential information without being too large. What does "compact" mean in this context?

hintAnswer: One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
title: Choosing the Right Encoding
text: Which encoding strategy allows you to capture the information of each codon while keeping the representation manageable?
choices: Apply one one hot encoding to the entire DNA string.
One hot encode each of the 1,000 disjoint codons, per sample.
One hot encode each of the $$500$$ disjoint $$6$$ letter combinations, per sample.
Bag of words encoding, where each "word" is a codon
